correctness.rationale: Every agent belongs to exactly one size bucket. With a_s fixed and b_s adjacent-size approvals, the number in bucket s equals a_s+b_s-t_s+t_{s-1}, and divisibility by s is necessary and sufficient because membership is otherwise unconstrained. The transition condition is exactly t_{s-1} congruent to t_s-a_s-b_s modulo s. For fixed current t_s, minimization (respectively maximization) of cumulative groups reduces to the minimum (maximum) of s times the prior count plus predecessor t_{s-1} in one residue class. The timestamped representative array costs O(sum_s(b_s+1))=O(n), with O(n) predecessors stored and O(n) witness construction. A standalone exact-integer verifier checked 2536 complete n<=4 approval profiles, 5000 seeded n=5..8 profiles against exhaustive labeled set partitions, and 1250 additional profiles by a second flexible-allocation enumerator. This is a proof for all n, supported but not replaced by finite tests; assumes O(log n)-bit word RAM arithmetic.

originality.rationale: The 2023 originating paper has an O(n^5) algorithm for all interval approvals and gives the nonconsecutive two-size modular orientation reformulation; these do not supply the stated O(n) optimizer of both group-count extrema in the consecutive-one-step subclass. The 2017 paper proves NP-completeness of general two-size approvals, but its separated-choice reduction does not apply to adjacent choices. Direct published-finding corpus searches for the source, adjacent-size aliases, modular orientations on paths, and group-count optimization returned no comparable exact statement. Thus best-knowledge originality holds, with acknowledged risk of unlocated equivalent specialized algorithms.

value.rationale: For a natural real scheduling interpretation of Woeginger's hiking problem, each participant approves a single preferred group size and optionally the next neighboring size. This smallest nontrivial approval uncertainty retains the combinatorial divisibility challenge but admits a structural one-step carry and a sharp linear-time algorithm computing feasibility, both possible group-count extremes and actual partitions. The shift from an O(n^5) general-interval feasibility algorithm to O(n) constructive extrema is mathematical, not just coding efficiency: it identifies why path-adjacent choice labels avoid the NP-hard arbitrary-pair obstruction. No assumption or claim about all intermediate group counts or all wider intervals is made.
